title: Oxidation–reduction reactions
competency: Identify oxidation, reduction and the agents, find oxidation numbers, and balance redox equations by oxidation number and half-reaction methods.

keywords.def: Loss of electrons; the oxidation number increases.
Gain of electrons; the oxidation number decreases.
The species that is reduced: it takes electrons from another species.
The species that is oxidized: it gives electrons to another species.
The charge an atom would have if all its bonds were ionic. Elements are 0.
A reaction in which electrons move from one species to another, so oxidation and reduction happen together.
The oxidation part or the reduction part of a redox reaction, written with electrons.

en.text: Oxidation is loss of electrons (oxidation number goes up); reduction is gain of electrons (oxidation number goes down). They always happen together in a redox reaction. The oxidizing agent is the species reduced; the reducing agent is the species oxidized. Oxidation numbers add up to 0 in a compound and to the charge in an ion.

screens.title: Magnesium in acid
screens.ask: A magnesium ribbon fizzes in hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. What happens to the Mg atoms?
opts: They lose electrons and become Mg²⁺
screens.after: Mg goes from 0 to +2: it loses two electrons (oxidation). H⁺ gains them and becomes H₂ (reduction).

screens.title: Oxidation and reduction
paras: Oxidation: loss of electrons; the oxidation number increases.
Reduction: gain of electrons; the oxidation number decreases.
They always occur together, so we call them redox reactions.
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂: Mg 0 → +2 (oxidized), H +1 → 0 (reduced). Cl⁻ is a spectator.

screens.title: Agents and oxidation numbers
paras: The oxidizing agent takes electrons, so it is reduced.
The reducing agent gives electrons, so it is oxidized.
Elements: 0. O: usually −2. H: usually +1. Group 1 metals: +1.
The numbers add to 0 in a compound and to the charge in an ion.

screens.title: Redox or not?
screens.why: A reaction is redox only if some oxidation numbers change.
screens.clue: Look for an element on one side and an ion on the other.

Hg²⁺ is oxidized; N₂H₄ is reduced

screens.why: Hg: +2 → 0 (gain). N: −2 → 0 (loss).

ideas.name: Balancing by change in oxidation number

en.text: To balance a redox equation by oxidation numbers: assign oxidation numbers, find which atoms change and by how many electrons, multiply so that electrons lost equal electrons gained, use the multipliers as coefficients, and finish the other atoms by inspection.

am.text: በኦክሳይዴሽን ቁጥር ለውጥ ማመጣጠን፡ የጠፉ ኤሌክትሮኖች ከተቀበሉት ጋር እኩል እንዲሆኑ አባዛ፣ ቀሪውን በምልከታ አመጣጥን።

screens.title: How many electrons?
screens.ask: PbS + O₂ → PbO + SO₂. Sulfur goes from −2 in PbS to +4 in SO₂. How many electrons does each S lose?
screens.after: From −2 to +4 is a rise of 6, so each S loses 6 electrons.

screens.title: Six steps
paras: 1. Write the unbalanced equation.
2. Assign oxidation numbers.
3. Find the atoms oxidized and reduced.
4. Count electrons lost and gained.
5. Multiply so electrons lost = electrons gained; use the factors as coefficients.
6. Balance the rest by inspection.

screens.why: N in HNO₃ is +5; in NO it is +2. A fall in oxidation number is a gain of electrons.

screens.why: Each S loses 6e⁻; each O₂ gains 4e⁻. 2 S lose 12e⁻, so 3 O₂.
Cl gains 6e⁻ (+5 → −1); each Br loses 1e⁻, so 6 Br.
S loses 2e⁻, N gains 3e⁻: 3 S and 2 N. H: 6 + 2 = 8, so 4H₂O.

en.text: Split the reaction into an oxidation half and a reduction half. Balance atoms other than O and H, then O with H₂O, then H with H⁺, then charge with electrons. Multiply so the electrons cancel and add the halves. In basic solution, finish as if acidic, then add OH⁻ equal to the H⁺ to both sides and turn H⁺ + OH⁻ into H₂O.

am.text: በግማሽ ግብረመልስ ዘዴ፡ O በH₂O፣ H በH⁺፣ ቻርጅ በኤሌክትሮን አመጣጥን፤ ኤሌክትሮኖቹ እንዲሰረዙ አባዛ።

screens.title: Where do the electrons go?
screens.ask: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺. To balance the charge, where do we write the electron?
opts: On the right, as a product
On the left, as a reactant
screens.after: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻. In oxidation the electrons are products; in reduction they are reactants.

screens.title: Half-reaction steps (acidic)
paras: 1. Split into oxidation and reduction halves.
2. Balance atoms other than O and H.
3. Balance O with H₂O, then H with H⁺.
4. Balance charge with e⁻.
5. Multiply so electrons are equal; add; check atoms and charge.
Basic solution: add OH⁻ equal to H⁺ to both sides; H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; cancel water.

screens.title: Dichromate and iron(II)
steps: Reduction: Cr₂O₇²⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O; add 14H⁺; charge +12 vs +6, so add 6e⁻.
Multiply the iron half by 6 and add: 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ → 6Fe³⁺ + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O.

screens.text: To finish a half-reaction balance in basic solution you
opts: add OH⁻ equal to the H⁺ to both sides
remove all H⁺ from one side

screens.why: Then each H⁺ + OH⁻ becomes H₂O and extra water cancels.
